1.explanation:
• TimePicker/TimePicker.mdx & TimePicker/docs/overview.mdx: These two files define the public API, usage examples, and visual specs for the TimePicker component itself. They will show the existing props and styling hooks where the new `readOnly` prop and styles should be added.
• TextInput/TextInput.mdx & TextInput/docs/overview.mdx: The hh:mm field is implemented as a TextInput under the hood. To make it read‐only, you need to see how the TextInput handles a `readOnly` prop (or lacks it) and apply matching CSS tokens and class names.
• Select/Select.mdx & Select/docs/overview.mdx: The AM/PM and timezone selectors are built on the Select component. Examining its API and styling will guide how to pass a `readOnly` state and disable the dropdown caret while preserving layout and border.

Together, these six documents give you the component APIs, markup structure, style tokens, and spacing rules necessary to implement, style, test, and document the new read-only variant of TimePicker in React, as well as to build the accompanying story and RTL tests.
1.bug_scenario:
The images illustrate the TimePicker in its “no‐input” (empty) and “filled” states and show the design specifications for a new "read‐only" variant. The component is composed of:
• A TextInput field for the “hh:mm” placeholder or time value
• Two dropdown selects (one for AM/PM, one for timezone) with caret icons
• A label (“Choose a time”) on the left
• A transparent background and a 1px border around each segment

The first image surfaces the color tokens ($text-secondary, $text-primary, $text-placeholder, $icon-disabled, $border-strong-01) and the transparent background. The second image describes the spacing and sizing (40px/2.5rem height, 1px borders, 16px horizontal gutters) that the read-only version must preserve.
